editorial:
Imagine you are a top surgeon who has spent your whole life trying to forget a painful family history. That is exactly where you find Simone. He lives a fancy, quiet life in Italy until one night he sees a man hurt in the street. When Simone sees a Nazi tattoo on the guy, he makes a split-second choice to leave him there to die. It is a heavy start that puts you right in the middle of a moral battle. You will feel the guilt eating away at him as he tries to make things right by helping the man's children, including a teen son who actually shares those same hateful views. 

The acting is solid and keeps you invested in whether Simone can actually find peace. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow. It is not an action movie, but the tension builds up nicely until the final confrontation. If you enjoy stories about forgiveness and secrets, you should definitely check this out. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV to see all the detail in those moody Italian streets. It is a great pick for a quiet night in.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when Marica finds out that Simone was the one who left her father to die. She comes to his house seeking revenge, but the movie turns into a lesson about breaking the cycle of hate. Instead of more violence, the film shows that holding onto anger only hurts the survivor. Simone faces the consequences of his choice, and the family has to decide if they can move past the tragedy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories about morality and family secrets.
